documents.unit: Office of the Provost and Executive VP for Academic Affairs
documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Academic Contexts
documents.summary: Provost-issued university policy (aligned with BOR Policy 6.28) covering AI in teaching, research and administration. It gives faculty academic freedom to use, forbid or structure AI in their courses, requires each syllabus to carry an AI statement, and sets data, tool-vetting, training and governance rules. It treats unauthorized AI-generated submissions as plagiarism and agentic completion of assessments as cheating.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no university-wide rule on student AI use. It says "faculty are free to use, not use, or otherwise structure the use of AI within their courses as they see fit" and requires a syllabus statement sorting uses into "forbidden, restricted, and permitted". The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates, although a Flexible AI Statement Builder is offered as a template.

units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.policy: All students, faculty, and staff should be familiar with and comply with the University and University System of Georgia policies that govern the use of AI, including but not limited to the University Academic Dishonesty Policy, the Code of Student Conduct, FERPA and the USG Artificial Intelligence Guidelines.

units.resolution_why: Found only by A. "The provost shall appoint the Committee members" and the membership list say who the review body is. It is a real governance rule, so kept; P54 is the closest type because the committee is the policy's review body.

units.resolution_why: A coded course-start and B before-course. The statement is a communication to students, so course-start.

units.policy: Data classified as Confidential (Class 1) or Sensitive (Class 2) should only be provided to AI models that are listed in the approved inventory of AI tools.
units.resolution_why: A coded general and B during-work. It tells users where to send classified data when using AI, so during-work.

units.why: "Academic Affairs will lead professional development opportunities for faculty and staff" supports faculty in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: Academic Affairs will lead professional development opportunities for faculty and staff
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance encourage and B neutral. The sentence commits to PD on "effective integration into teaching and research", which welcomes AI use, so encourage.

units.why: "Students will have access to additional educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools, promote responsible usage, and highlight potential risks" offers AI education to students. P63 is about supporting faculty, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools
units.uncovered_note: University-provided AI education programs for students (not faculty support).
units.resolution_why: A coded P63 (nearest type) and B coded UNCOVERED. P63 is defined as support for instructors; programs for students are not covered, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: Researchers "are required to stay informed about emerging AI tools and evolving best practices" is a research duty (P62).
units.anchor: required to stay informed about emerging AI tools and evolving best practices
units.resolution_why: A coded general and B during-work. Staying informed about tools is a standing duty, not an act of doing the work, so general.

units.why: "The following types of data must not be entered into public AI tools" lists restricted research data. P50 because the rule is about privacy even though it sits in the research section.
units.anchor: The following types of data must not be entered into public AI tools
units.resolution_why: A coded prohibit/general and B restrict/during-work. The list bars listed data from public tools but leaves AI use allowed, so restrict; it is a conduct rule for the research process, so during-work.

units.why: "Researchers are responsible for independently verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content" is a verification duty (P31).
units.anchor: independently verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content
units.resolution_why: A coded general and B during-work. Verification happens when using AI output, so during-work.

units.why: "Researchers should take steps to identify and mitigate known issues of bias" names bias in outputs (P53).
units.anchor: identify and mitigate known issues of bias in AI-generated outputs
units.resolution_why: A coded general and B during-work. Mitigating bias is part of using outputs, so during-work.

units.why: "the IRB will review the use of the AI tool" when AI touches human-participant data; governs AI in research (P62).
units.anchor: the IRB will review the use of the AI tool
units.resolution_why: A coded informs/general and B must/during-work. The sentence says what the IRB will do ("the IRB will review the use of the AI tool"), a statement of process, so informs and general.

units.why: "Disclose the use of AI in the project and IRB application" requires research disclosure; P62 chosen over P24 because it is a research-governance step.
units.anchor: Disclose the use of AI in the project and IRB application

units.why: Consent documents "must explain the purpose and use of AI understandably and transparently", a participant-protection rule in research (P62).
units.anchor: Informed consent documents must explain the purpose and use of AI
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. "Informed consent documents must explain the purpose and use of AI understandably and transparently" is a separate research rule from the disclosure bullet before it, so kept (P62).

units.why: "Review and understand the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy of the software before using it" is a terms-of-use duty for research tools (P52).
units.anchor: Review and understand the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy
units.resolution_why: A coded before-course and B during-work. Researchers review the terms before using the software, a step in doing the research, so during-work. before-course means course design.

units.why: "Utilize AI models that are listed in the approved inventory or seek ITS approval before use with non-public data" ties research tools to vetted ones (P50).
units.anchor: Utilize AI models that are listed in the approved inventory

units.why: "University members must inform themselves and comply with journal and funding agency policies regarding the use of AI" defers AI research rules to outside venues, so P62.
units.anchor: must inform themselves and comply with journal and funding agency policies
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (A's nearby unit is the next sentence, on disclosure and citation). The sentence is a separate rule that members must follow journal and funder AI policies, so kept (P62).

units.why: AI assistance in research "must be appropriately disclosed and cited" per venue and funder rules. P62 over P24 because it targets research venues.
units.anchor: must be appropriately disclosed and cited following disciplinary, journal, and funding agency requirements
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B's nearby unit is a different sentence about complying with venue policies). "AI assistance in research ... must be appropriately disclosed and cited" is a disclosure rule for research, so kept as P62 (not P24, which is for submissions).

units.why: "Name the AI tool used, its specific version, and the date range" is minimum documentation naming tool and date (P25).
units.anchor: Name the AI tool used, its specific version, and the date range
units.resolution_why: A coded must and B should. The list is introduced by "Minimum documentation for all researchers should include:", so should.

units.why: "Detail how the AI tool was used ... and the extent of AI's contribution" requires stating how and how much AI contributed (P24).
units.anchor: Detail how the AI tool was used
units.resolution_why: A coded must and B should. The list is introduced by "should include", so should.

units.why: "Confirm that only approved AI tools were used with confidential, sensitive, restricted, or personal identifiable information" is a required data-privacy confirmation (P50).
units.anchor: Confirm that only approved AI tools were used
units.resolution_why: A coded must and B should. The list is introduced by "should include", so should.

units.why: "Evidence of human oversight of the process and review of all AI output" is required documentation of human review (P31).
units.anchor: Evidence of human oversight of the process and review of all AI output
units.resolution_why: A coded must and B should. The list is introduced by "should include", so should.

units.why: "Consider including the specific prompts or queries" is optional documentation of prompts, listed under what documentation "may also include" (P25).
units.anchor: Consider including the specific prompts or queries provided to the AI system

units.why: Optional documentation "describing the process of human review, editing, and factchecking of the AI-generated content" documents verification (P31).
units.anchor: Documentation describing the process of human review, editing, and factchecking
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. "Documentation describing the process of human review, editing, and factchecking" is an optional documentation item in the 'may also include' list, a separate rule from the sentence after it, so kept (P31, may).

units.why: The documentation item "This should explicitly affirm human responsibility and accountability for the final content" says what the human-review documentation must show about ownership of the result. It is an accountability rule (P29), separate from the description of the review process in the sentence before it.
units.anchor: explicitly affirm human responsibility and accountability for the final content
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (A's unit on the same item is the review-process sentence before it, coded P31 and may). This sentence is a separate rule on affirming responsibility, so kept (P29, should).

units.why: Researchers "engaging with external collaborators using AI tools should follow the guidelines" extends the rules to collaborations (P62).
units.anchor: engaging with external collaborators using AI tools should follow the guidelines
units.resolution_why: A coded general and B during-work. The guidance applies to researchers' collaborations in practice, so during-work.

units.why: "It is the responsibility of the supervising faculty member to ensure that their students and post-doctoral fellows complete the required training" is a duty to see that mandatory training is done. It is not support for faculty learning AI (P63), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: responsibility of the supervising faculty member to ensure that their students
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).
units.resolution_why: A coded P63 and B coded UNCOVERED. The duty is to enforce completion of mandatory training, which no type covers, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: "Information Technology Services will serve as the point of contact for operational or non-academic questions, including data classification, software approvals, and security incidents." assigns a contact point in the framework, so P56 like the Provost contact.
units.anchor: Information Technology Services will serve as the point of contact
units.resolution_why: Found only by A, who coded P54. It is a real assignment of responsibility, so kept; coded P56 to match the other points of contact, since it says nothing about reviewing the policy.

units.why: The Office of Student Conduct "will serve as the point of contact for all questions related to the Academic Dishonesty policy and use of AI", directing integrity matters (P36).
units.anchor: Office of Student Conduct will serve as the point of contact

documents.title: Academic Affairs Policies record 51 (abstract page)
documents.summary: Repository abstract page for the university AI policy. It repeats only the purpose statement of the full policy and adds no new rules.
documents.stance_why: The page states only a purpose ("responsible, ethical, and transparent use") and sets no stance on student AI use itself. The full policy it points to delegates to faculty, so delegates.

units.why: The abstract states the policy aim: "responsible, ethical, and transparent use" of AI across teaching, research and administration, "encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy". It is an institution-wide framework or preamble (P56). It repeats the other document but is coded on its own.
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools
units.resolution_why: Both coders found the purpose sentence and coded P56/all/general/informs. B also split off the clause 'while encouraging innovation, academic freedom, and appropriate autonomy' as P04. That clause is part of the same purpose sentence and sets no separate rule, so it was dropped and the purpose unit covers it.

notes: Reconciled from coderA and coderB. Both coders gave stance delegates for both documents. Mandatory AI training (students, staff, all members, supervisors) fits no type and is coded UNCOVERED; a new type for required AI training is suggested for the codebook memo. Compliance recordkeeping is also UNCOVERED. The Digital Commons abstract page repeats the purpose sentence. The source has a typo 'Al AI tools used' that the fragment 'Al AI tools used in the' reproduces. Points of contact for Research Integrity and the Dean of Students were coded by neither coder and were left out.
